source: Make a game where you spawn in with a lobby, in the lobby theres invis barriers with the roads, theres gonna be things u can walk into, theres gonna be 2 1 player gamemodes, 2 player, 3 player and 4 player, once u go in that space and the timers done u load in the game, Its a different experience, The game will be called Silenced , And the thumbnail will be a Janitor with tiny red patches on his uniform, then back to when ur in the things and the game loads, your gonna load in a REALISTIC school, you can interact with SOME students, its about people going missing, it will be a game where the janitor cleans up and its gonna be a STORY MODE, The janitor gets laughed at and gets rubbish thrown at him, theres tasks he does around the school, like cleaning the toilets, classes, and the big halls, the school gonna be 3 story, and make SOME classrooms with all the chairs and tables packed away like schools over, but make a few students be scattered around the school asleep, and make there be rich kids that act like theyre the principil, but yeah the games called Silenced, And also make there be toilets that are out of order and make the bathroom be flooding a bit from the stalls

image_prompt.text: The doorway out of each mode-entry space, marking the transition from the lobby chapter into the school
The school entrance opening onto the full three-storey atrium so the building reads at first sight
One-way transitions that stop the player wandering back into a finished part of the story
The lobby all players spawn into, with roads running through it, sized for a full server
The spaces you walk into to queue for a mode, which load everyone into the school when the timer finishes
A realistic three-storey school: classrooms, corridors, big halls and toilet blocks
Some classrooms with all the chairs and tables packed away as if school is over
Out-of-order toilets with water flooding a little way out from the stalls
Rubbish and litter through the corridors for the janitor to clean

layout_placement.text: Mode-entry volumes that hold players on a countdown and then move them into the school map
Invisible barriers running along the lobby roads
Separate one, two, three and four player mode-entry spaces
Cleaning task stations: toilets, classrooms and the big halls
Student NPC positions, some interactive, some asleep and scattered around the school, plus rich kids who act like they run the place

notes: Lobby and school cannot co-exist on one surface, so this is a Chaptered Journey and routes P4. Within the school itself the layout is open rather than corridor-linear, which the shape does not express.

The lobby is Party and Casual and the school is Adventure. Adventure is dominant because the prompt calls it a story mode, so the lobby only contributes options and its Lobby-and-Isolated-Stage shape was dropped even though it describes half the build.
A three-storey interior needs interior generation and probably tiered or overhanging handling, but no loaded option carries the building, so the pipeline does not reflect that cost.
No option covers the mode-entry pads, the invisible barriers, the NPC students or the cleaning task stations; all ride as id-null entries.

open_questions.ask: What ends a run: finishing the task list, surviving to the end of the shift, or reaching a story beat about the missing people?
Do the one, two, three and four player modes use the same school map, or four different maps?
How big is the school: a few corridors per floor, or a full campus with grounds?

theme: Modern Urban, explicitly realistic present-day school

coverage_missing.ask: What ends a round or completes the story?
Do the four player-count modes share one school map or use different ones?
Is the school a single building or a campus with grounds?
Where do the lobby roads go, and are the invisible barriers there to keep players on foot paths or to fence the lobby in?

answers.ask: What ends a run: finishing the task list, surviving to the end of the shift, or reaching a story beat about the missing people?
answers.answer: A run ends when the players finish the janitor task list for the shift, with the missing-people story unfolding through the story mode as they do it.

answers.ask: Do the one, two, three and four player modes use the same school map, or four different maps?
answers.answer: All player-count modes use the same realistic three-story school map; the lobby spaces only set how many players load into that experience.

answers.ask: How big is the school: a few corridors per floor, or a full campus with grounds?
answers.answer: Keep it to a compact three-story school with a few corridors per floor, including classrooms, halls, and bathrooms, rather than a full campus with grounds.
